notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR1: 'If more than one COBOL library is available during compilation, text-name-1 must be qualified by library-name-1 identifying the COBOL library in which the text associated with text-name-1 resides. Within one COBOL library, each text-name must be unique.' The second sentence holds: CopyProcessor#LocateInLibrary takes the first file of the name and suffix list, so a text-name names one text in a library (DOC-A.1-40). The first holds since kb/Work PB5473 (landed): which libraries are available is the implementor's to say, and the DOC-A.1-40 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7) states it, the default library and each library a COPY statement of the compilation group names with OF or IN that a library place holds (FindCopybook reports it); CopyProcessor#CountLibraries refuses at 85 every unqualified COPY of a group that names such a library, wherever it stands (one met before the first named library waits for it), through the constructs row copy-unqualified-text-name-2002 (COBOL0900; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex F.2 item 38 lets the default library's text go unqualified). Probe c1.cob (MSGTXT.cpy and LIBB/MSGTXT.cpy; COPY MSGTXT. COPY MSGTXT OF LIBB. COPY MSGTXT IN LIBB.): COBOL0900 at the unqualified COPY at 85, DEFAULT TEXT / LIBB TEXT / LIBB TEXT at 2002. Witnesses: pb5473-copy-every-text-qualified (85: LIBRARY A, LIBRARY B), pb5473-copy-unqualified-text-name (refused at 85), and 1985-SR-XII_2_3-1 (one library, unqualified, accepted).

next.reason: 'Within one COBOL library, each text-name must be unique' is kept by §2023:7.2.3.3 SR3, and library-name-1 still identifies the library holding the text (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR2). But 1985 requires text-name-1 to be qualified by library-name-1 whenever more than one library is available; 2023 has no such rule: 'When neither library-name-1 nor literal-2 is specified, a default COBOL library is used' (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR3). An unqualified COPY that 1985 refused with several libraries is accepted in 2023. Looser.
